decisions.reason: As a security-oriented communication add-on close to the firm's core capabilities, it is likely to be retained while management waits for clearer evidence on customer uptake.
The mobile PDF signature function fits growing business demand for digital workflows, so absent clear underperformance a medium-sized established firm would usually keep it for another year.
This product is strongly aligned with the firm's core security and consultancy business, making it likely to stay unless results fall well below aspiration levels.
Its niche workflow and integration requirements make it more uncertain, but with no explicit failure signal the firm would likely continue to test the market rather than withdraw immediately.

A hardware-based signature token sits less naturally with a software consultancy firm's resource base, so if early results are merely uncertain or below aspiration management is more likely to reallocate resources elsewhere.
A payment security compliance suite matches enterprise demand and the firm's established competencies, so behavioral theory suggests retention while performance information accumulates.
